fdroid:app.devswitch.name: DevSwitch
fdroid:app.devswitch.summary: Toggle developer options, USB and wireless debugging, with Quick Settings tiles
fdroid:app.devswitch.description:
DevSwitch turns Developer options, USB debugging and Wireless debugging on and off from one screen, three Quick Settings tiles, a home screen widget, and shortcuts on the app icon. It writes the same system settings Android's own Settings app does, so the system reacts immediately: adbd starts or stops, and the Developer options screen appears or hides.
One-time setup
Android only lets an app change these settings if it holds WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS, which cannot be requested with a dialog. Grant it once, in any of three ways, and it survives reboots and updates:
- From a computer: adb shell pm grant app.devswitch android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
- On the phone, through Shizuku, with no computer needed
- With root
Wireless tab
Shows this device's IP address and its live wireless debugging address, plus a scan of adb devices on the Wi-Fi. With Shizuku running it also lists paired computers and can pair a new one, either by showing a code for adb pair or by scanning the QR that Android Studio shows.
Safety
Turning a switch off, or unpairing a computer, asks first, because either can cut the connection a computer is using. The tiles, the widget and the shortcuts do nothing while the phone is locked.
Privacy
No network services, no accounts, no analytics. The only network use is local discovery of adb devices on your own Wi-Fi.
Free software under the GPLv3.

fdroid:com.siarheikuchuk.ftpsserver.name: FTPS Server
fdroid:com.siarheikuchuk.ftpsserver.summary: Run a secure FTP server and share files on your local network, with no ads.
fdroid:com.siarheikuchuk.ftpsserver.description:
FTPS Server turns your phone or tablet into a secure FTP server for private file sharing. Share photos, videos, and documents with a computer on the same Wi-Fi, without uploading them to a cloud. You choose who can connect, which folder they can open, and whether they can only download files or also change them.
 Share files on your network, not through a cloud 
 Files stay on your Android device. The other device connects to this FTP server over your own network, so a copy is not sitting on someone else's storage.
 Move photos, videos, and documents from your phone to a PC, or from a PC onto your phone.
 Keep personal and work files off third-party cloud storage.
 Use it at home, in an office, or on a hotspot you control. The client has to be on the same network: the same Wi-Fi, or the same hotspot or USB tethering link.
 Leave the server running with the screen off. A notification keeps transfers going.
 Choose who can open which folder 
 Add a separate login for each person or device, and limit what that login can do.
 Create a username and password for every connection.
 Give each login its own folder. That login cannot browse the rest of the files on your device.
 Allow full access, or a read-only login that can download files but cannot upload, rename, or delete.
 Copy or share the address, port, and logins when the other device is ready to connect.
 Encrypted transfer, not plain FTP 
 This is an FTPS server: explicit FTP over TLS (AUTH TLS). Plain FTP, with no encryption, is not used. The password and the files are encrypted while they cross the network.
 A login is not sent in the clear. Transfers use FTP over TLS.
 The first start creates a TLS certificate for you, so you can connect without extra setup.
 If you already have a certificate, you can use that instead.
 Compare the certificate fingerprint shown in the app with the one shown by your client, so you know you reached this device.
 File names in your own language are preserved, including letters that are not in the English alphabet.
 See what the server is doing 
 The app shows the address and port to enter in the client.
 Each login is listed with its folder and whether access is read-only or full.
 A log shows connection activity when something fails and you need to see why.
 You choose the port and how many clients can be connected at once.
 Start the FTP server in four steps 
 1. Add a user, with a username and a password.
2. Pick the folder that user is allowed to open.
3. Choose read-only or full access.
4. On the other device, open an FTPS client, turn on explicit TLS (AUTH TLS), and enter the address, port, and login.
 Clients that can connect 
 Any client that supports explicit FTPS works. Examples: FileZilla and WinSCP on Windows, FileZilla on Linux, Cyberduck or FileZilla on Mac, and an FTPS client on another phone.
 Typical uses 
 Copy files between a phone and a laptop on the same Wi-Fi.
 Open phone files from a desktop file manager.
 Hand someone a read-only login when they should download files and nothing else.
 What this FTP server is not 
 It does not upload your files to the developer or to a cloud service. It is also not a public file host. Use it on a network you trust, such as home or office Wi-Fi.
 FTPS Server is open source (CC0-1.0) and contains no ads.

fdroid:me.diamondforge.tokn.name: Tokn - MFA / 2FA authenticator
fdroid:me.diamondforge.tokn.summary: Open-source 2FA authenticator. Encrypted on-device. No accounts.
fdroid:me.diamondforge.tokn.description:
Tokn is a small, privacy-first 2FA / MFA authenticator. Your one-time codes stay on your device, encrypted. No accounts, no cloud sync, no analytics, no ads.
A simple, open-source TOTP / HOTP authenticator for people who do not want their second factor in someone else's cloud.
WHY TOKN
• Private by design. No sign-up, no telemetry, and no Google Play Services on your device.
• Encrypted vault. Stored in an SQLCipher database, unlocked with biometrics (fingerprint or face) or a password.
• Works fully offline. Codes are generated locally on your phone.
• Open source. GPL-3.0, source available on GitHub, also published on F-Droid.
FEATURES
• TOTP and HOTP support per RFC 6238 and RFC 4226
• SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512
• Add accounts by scanning a QR code with the camera or from a gallery image
• Manual entry for codes you cannot scan
• Biometric unlock with password fallback
• Encrypted backup and restore for moving to a new phone or keeping a copy
• Device-to-device sync over local Wi-Fi, Wi-Fi Direct or animated QR code. Nothing leaves your network and the handshake is end-to-end encrypted
• Organize accounts with custom groups, multiple groups per account
• Recycle Bin that keeps deleted items optionally for 30d. Configurable
• Audit Log to see your vault actions
• Custom icons and importable icon packs (Aegis-compatible)
• Material 3 design with light, dark or system theme and optional Material You colors
• Screenshot protection keeps codes out of the recents preview and blocks screen capture
SWITCHING FROM ANOTHER 2FA APP
Tokn imports backups from Aegis, 2FAS, Google Authenticator and standard otpauth:// URIs. Bring your existing accounts over in minutes.
WORKS WITH
Any service that supports standard TOTP or HOTP two-factor authentication. Google, GitHub, GitLab, Microsoft, Amazon, Discord, Twitch, Reddit, Dropbox, Proton, and thousands more.
LICENSE
Tokn is free software, released under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later.
Website with comparisons and migration guides:
https://usetokn.app
Source code, releases and issue tracker:
https://github.com/tokn-authenticator/tokn

Birdtray is a system tray new mail notification for Thunderbird, which does not require extensions
 Features:
 Shows the unread email counter in the Thunderbird system tray icon.
 Optionally can animate the Thunderbird system tray icon if new mail is received.
 You can snooze new mail notifications for a specific time period.

 Can monitor that Thunderbird is running, and indicate it if you accidentally closed it.
 Has configurable "New Email" functionality, allowing pre-configured email templates.
 The feature to "Start Thunderbird when Birdtray starts" needs the flathub thunderbird installed by default. The default thunderbird directory is "~/.var/app/org.mozilla.Thunderbird/.thunderbird".

firefox-addons:3044797.description:
Find out what any webpage really loads: the trackers and pixels, cookies, third-party scripts, API calls and technologies behind it, each with the evidence Firefox captured. Free. No account. The analysis runs in your browser.
Open a page, click the PageScanner icon, and five reports are ready:
- Tech Stack: what the website is built with
- Privacy: which trackers, pixels and cookies are on the page, and where its data goes
- PCI DSS: which scripts run on a payment page (Requirement 6.4.3)
- AppSec: a 0 to 100 front-end security score with findings and fixes
- APIs: which endpoints the page calls, and from which script
Export any report as JSON, Excel, PDF, Word or HTML for your team, your client or your auditor.
NEW IN VERSION 6
- Rebuilt around five reports, each answering one question, in one popup.
- Full-screen flow reports that trace scripts and API calls back to their source.
- Export to JSON, Excel, PDF, Word and interactive HTML.
- Page history per tab: step back through earlier pages with Prev and Next.
- Light and dark mode, private-window support, and a notice for managed installs.
WHO USES IT
- Privacy officers and counsel: see which trackers and cookies a page loads, accept or reject the consent banner, reload, and export both reports to compare. Useful for GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, HIPAA and CIPA reviews.
- PCI DSS merchants and assessors: list every script observed on a payment page, first-party or third-party, with Content Security Policy, Subresource Integrity and nonce checks marked Pass, Warn or Fail.
- Security engineers and developers: scan a staging or production page before release and read the score, missing headers, risky scripts and outdated JavaScript libraries. Intranet, localhost and local files work too.
- Marketers, agencies and analysts: look up a competitor's tech stack, or audit your own site for leftover tags and pixels.
- Vendor risk and GRC teams: see which third parties a site connects to, and in which countries, before you sign or renew.
FIVE REPORTS, FIVE QUESTIONS
1. Tech Stack: what is this site built with? Technologies, products and vendors observed on the page or across the website, grouped by category, with the evidence and version where observed.
2. Privacy: who collects data on this page? Trackers, pixels and data brokers by name and category, cookies, web forms that collect personal data, and a map of the countries the page connects to.
3. PCI DSS: which scripts load on my payment page? A script inventory with first-party, third-party, inline and eval counts for PCI DSS 4.0.1 Requirement 6.4.3, and integrity checks relevant to Requirement 11.6.1. It is evidence from your visit, not an audit result.
4. AppSec: how exposed is the front end? A 0 to 100 score from a formula shown in the product, findings grouped from Transport Security to injection signals with evidence and recommendations, and JavaScript libraries matched against a bundled vulnerability database.
5. APIs: what does this page call? Observed API endpoints with their HTTP method, telemetry and noise kept apart, and a flow report linking each call to the script or vendor where attribution is available.
HOW IT WORKS
1. Add PageScanner to Firefox and pin it to the toolbar. There is nothing to set up.
2. Open a website. Each page is scanned as it loads, and the icon shows a count for the current tab.
3. Click the icon. Switch between the five reports, open any finding for its evidence, and export.
DEPLOY ACROSS YOUR FLEET
Roll PageScanner out through Firefox enterprise policies like any other add-on. No license keys, no account, no server. Force-install it with policies.json (ExtensionSettings) or the Firefox ADMX templates, using the add-on ID pagescanner@feroot.com and its addons.mozilla.org install URL. Managed installs show a one-line managed notice. Deployment guide: https://www.feroot.com/feroot-pagescanner/deployment-guide/ 
PRIVACY
Analysis runs in your browser against databases bundled inside the extension. The extension sends no browsing data and no scan results to Feroot, has no telemetry and runs no remote code. Deep Scan reads a page's own script files from their original hosts for closer analysis; switch to Light Scan in Settings to skip that. Cookie values and the text you type into forms are not put in reports, and exports redact URL query values and path parameters.
To scan private windows, allow PageScanner in private windows in the Add-ons Manager. Private observations stay in memory and are removed when the last private window closes.
When you uninstall PageScanner, Firefox opens a short, optional feedback form on Google Forms. The extension adds nothing about you to its address.
WHY DOES FIREFOX ASK FOR ACCESS TO ALL WEBSITES?
To observe what runs on a page, the scanner has to run on that page. PageScanner uses this access only to observe and report on the pages you visit, locally.
PCI DSS is a standard of the PCI Security Standards Council. PageScanner is not affiliated with or endorsed by the PCI SSC and does not certify compliance.

firefox-addons:2980371.name: Accessibility Persona Lens
firefox-addons:2980371.summary: Simulate accessibility barriers using GOV.UK personas to understand how different users experience the web.
firefox-addons:2980371.description:
Understand accessibility barriers by experiencing them firsthand.
Accessibility Persona Lens helps designers, developers, and product teams build empathy for users with different access needs. Based on the official GOV.UK Accessibility Personas developed by the Government Digital Service, this extension simulates real interaction barriers — not to replicate lived experiences, but to reveal friction points in your designs.
7 Personas, 7 Perspectives
Each persona represents a real pattern of web usage:
Claudia — Screen magnifier user with partial sight. Simulates 400% zoom, inverted colours, and highlighted focus.
Ashleigh — Screen reader user who is severely sight impaired. Applies heavy blur to encourage screen reader testing.
Ron — Older user with arthritis, hearing loss, and cataracts. Simulates mild visual impairment and motor difficulties.
Chris — Keyboard-only user with colour vision deficiency. Disables mouse interaction and applies greyscale.
Pawel — Autistic user sensitive to distractions. Adds visual and audio distractions to simulate concentration difficulties.
Simone — Dyslexic user. Applies dyslexia-friendly styling with letter scrambling to simulate reading challenges.
Saleem — Deaf user whose first language is BSL. Converts text to demonstrate reading in a second language.
Use Cases
Design reviews and accessibility audits
Developer testing and QA
Stakeholder demonstrations
Accessibility training workshops
Building team empathy
Privacy First
No data collection. No tracking. All preferences are stored locally on your device.
Important: These simulations demonstrate interaction barriers, not lived experiences. They are tools for understanding, not representations of disability.

firefox-addons:3052829.name: Only Shop
firefox-addons:3052829.summary: Hides Marketplace / third-party seller listings on popular Australian retailer sites, showing only products sold by the retailer.
firefox-addons:3052829.description:
Hides Marketplace / third-party seller listings on popular Australian retailer sites, showing only products sold by the retailer.
Only Shop hides Marketplace and third-party seller listings on Australian retailer websites - so search results only show products actually sold by the retailer.
Woolworths, Kmart, Big W, Bunnings, JB Hi-Fi and many more retailers all now run in-house marketplace programs that mix third-party seller listings into normal search and category pages. These listings often have longer delivery times, different return policies, and inconsistent quality compared to items sold directly by the retailer.
Only Shop finds and enforces each retailer's own way to exclude Marketplace listings, so you see only what the retailer itself sells and ships.
❓ How it works
Click the toolbar icon to see every supported retailer with its own on/off toggle - no need to be on that retailer's site to change it. The current site you're on is clearly marked, and the toolbar icon itself shows a green check when filtering is active, a red cross when it's off, so you always know the state at a glance.
Turning Only Shop off for a site doesn't force Marketplace listings back on or undo anything - it simply stops enforcing the filter, leaving the site exactly as it already was.
🛡 Privacy
Only Shop reads page URLs and rendered listings locally in your browser to apply each retailer's filter - none of that page content, your search terms, or your browsing activity is ever sent anywhere.
Only Shop can send anonymous, aggregate usage events (which retailer, and whether filtering was toggled on/off) to help understand what to maintain - this is on by default and can be turned off at any time from Settings in the popup.
ℹ Disclaimer
Only Shop is an independent, unofficial extension and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to any of the retailers listed above. It relies on each site's own markup and filters, which can change without notice - filtering may occasionally stop working or behave unexpectedly on a given site until updated.

apple-macos:733449447.name: Check ID Scanner
apple-macos:733449447.description:
Check ID is the fastest, most private, reliable way to scan and verify driver's licenses and IDs for events, venues, and guest management.
It reads the barcode on a driver’s license or state ID, checks the birth date and expiry date against your rules, and gives your staff a clear answer. What it keeps is a record that the check happened, never the details of who was checked.
WHAT A SCAN NEVER KEEPS
No name. No date of birth. No address. No ID number. No picture of the ID. Not in a scan record, on any plan. Guest lists are the one place names live, and only the names your staff add on purpose.
NO AD TRACKERS
No third-party analytics or advertising SDKs, no advertising identifier, and no ads. The app links two open-source libraries, both for reading passport chips. Our own product analytics tell us which features get used and what broke. They include coarse scan statistics, such as the result, the state and an age range, and never a name, birth date, address, ID number or photo.
A RECORD THAT THE CHECK HAPPENED
With Check ID for Teams, every scan is timestamped and signed by our server when it’s saved. Export a scan log (CSV) or a summary report (PDF), or share a report link. Reports never name your employees or the people who were checked.
CHECK ID FOR TEAMS
By default, staff check in with a PIN on shared iPhones and iPads at the door, so each scan records who ran it. Pair a door device from your own phone. Owners and managers review scans in the app or at app.checkidapp.com. One venue per plan; running several locations? Get in touch.
Repeat-entry alerts tell staff when the same ID is scanned again within your window, on any of your venue’s connected devices. It’s a prompt, not a block. They use a one-way code, re-keyed on our servers with a secret unique to your organization and deleted when the window closes. They start off by default for venues in New Hampshire, the EU and EEA, and countries we haven’t reviewed, and owners can change that per venue.
Guest lists and name search work from a copy on each device, so the door keeps going when the Wi-Fi doesn’t. Scans queue on the device and upload when the signal comes back.
WHAT IT READS
- The barcode on US and Canadian driver’s licenses and ID cards (the AAMVA PDF417 standard)
- The REAL ID indicator, when the barcode encodes one
- Many ePassports and chip ID cards, by reading the chip over NFC and checking its data against the issuing country’s certificates on our list (iPhone)
- Driver’s licenses and state IDs in Apple Wallet, through Apple’s own ID Verifier sheet (iPhone)
